# Residential Lease Agreement

**Premises:** 218 Elm Street, Unit 3, Halbrook, Ontario
**Landlord:** Orchard Lane Properties Inc.
**Tenant:** Jordan Avery
**Term:** September 1, 2026 to August 31, 2027

This agreement is made between Orchard Lane Properties Inc. (the Landlord) and Jordan Avery (the Tenant) for the rental of the premises described above. The parties agree to the terms set out in the sections that follow. Headings are for convenience and do not change the meaning of any section.

## 1. Definitions

"Premises" means the residential unit at 218 Elm Street, Unit 3, together with the storage locker numbered 3B in the basement and the parking space numbered 7 in the rear lot. "Building" means the structure at 218 Elm Street and the land it stands on. "Common areas" means the hallways, stairwells, laundry room, bicycle room, and rear lot. "Rent" means the monthly amount set out in section 4 and any other amount this agreement calls rent. "Business day" means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday, or a statutory holiday in Ontario.

## 2. Term

The tenancy begins on September 1, 2026 and ends on August 31, 2027. If neither party gives notice under section 17 before the end of the term, the tenancy continues month to month on the same terms, except that the Landlord may increase the rent as permitted by law. The Tenant receives the keys on the first day of the term once the first month's rent and the security deposit have cleared.

## 3. Occupants

The premises are occupied by the Tenant and by no more than one other adult and two children. A guest who stays more than fourteen nights in any sixty-day period is an occupant for the purposes of this section, and the Tenant must tell the Landlord that person's name in writing. The Tenant is responsible for the conduct of every occupant and guest.

## 4. Rent

Rent is $2,140 per month, due on the first day of each month. Rent is paid by pre-authorized debit from an account the Tenant names, or by electronic transfer to the address the Landlord gives in writing. Cash is not accepted. The Landlord issues a receipt for any payment on request and without charge.

## 5. Late payment

Rent not received by the end of the fifth day of the month is late. A late fee of $45 is charged for each month in which rent is late, and is added to the following month's rent. A payment returned by the Tenant's bank is charged a further $20 administration fee. Late fees are not charged for any month in which the Tenant and Landlord have agreed in writing, before the first of the month, to a later payment date.

## 6. Security deposit

The Tenant pays a security deposit of $2,140, equal to one month's rent, before the term begins. The Landlord holds it in a separate trust account and applies it to the last month's rent of the tenancy. The Landlord pays the Tenant interest on the deposit each year at the rate set by the province. The deposit is not a limit on what the Tenant owes for damage.

## 7. Utilities and services

Rent includes water, heat, and garbage collection. The Tenant pays for electricity and internet service, and opens accounts in their own name with Halbrook Hydro and with any internet provider they choose before the term begins. The Landlord maintains the building's shared laundry machines, which take a prepaid card sold at the property office. The Landlord does not guarantee any particular internet provider can serve the unit.

## 8. Use of the premises

The premises are used only as a private residence. The Tenant may work from home provided no clients or customers visit the premises and no goods are stored in the common areas. The Tenant does not sublet the premises or assign this agreement without the Landlord's written consent, which the Landlord does not withhold unreasonably. Short-term rental of any part of the premises through any platform is not permitted.

## 9. Pets

The Tenant may keep one cat or one dog under 25 kilograms. Before the animal moves in, the Tenant pays a one-time pet deposit of $350, which the Landlord holds with the security deposit and returns at the end of the tenancy less the cost of repairing any damage the animal caused. The Tenant keeps the animal leashed or carried in the common areas, cleans up after it in the rear lot, and keeps it from disturbing other residents. Fish in a tank under 40 litres and caged birds do not count as pets for this section.

## 10. Smoking

No one smokes or vapes any substance inside the premises, on the balcony, or in the common areas. Smoking is permitted only at the marked area at the north edge of the rear lot. The Tenant is responsible for the cost of removing smoke odour or staining caused by any occupant or guest.

## 11. Repairs and maintenance

The Landlord keeps the building and the premises in good repair and complies with health, safety, and housing standards. The Tenant reports any need for repair promptly through the maintenance portal at orchardlane.invalid/repairs, or by telephone at 555-0188 in an emergency. An emergency is a leak, a loss of heat between October 1 and May 31, a loss of power to the unit, a lock that will not secure the unit, or anything that makes the unit unsafe. The Landlord responds to an emergency within four hours and to any other request within five business days.

The Tenant keeps the premises clean, replaces light bulbs and furnace filters, tests the smoke and carbon monoxide alarms monthly, and repairs damage caused by any occupant or guest beyond normal wear and tear.

## 12. Alterations

The Tenant does not paint, install fixtures, change locks, or make any other alteration without the Landlord's written consent. Picture hooks and small nails for hanging pictures are permitted. A Tenant who installs an approved fixture removes it and repairs the wall at the end of the tenancy unless the Landlord agrees in writing to keep it.

## 13. Entry by the Landlord

The Landlord enters the premises only with written notice of at least twenty-four hours stating the reason and a time between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m., or without notice in an emergency, or when the Tenant agrees at the time. During the last sixty days of the tenancy, once either party has given notice to end it, the Landlord may show the premises to prospective tenants between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. after making a reasonable effort to tell the Tenant first.

## 14. Insurance

The Tenant keeps tenant's insurance for the whole tenancy, covering their own belongings and at least $1,000,000 in personal liability, and gives the Landlord proof of coverage before the term begins and at each renewal. The Landlord's insurance does not cover the Tenant's belongings.

## 15. Parking and storage

Parking space 7 is for one passenger vehicle with current plates. The Tenant does not repair vehicles, store fuel, or park trailers or boats in the rear lot. Storage locker 3B holds only household goods. Nothing flammable, perishable, or illegal is kept in the locker, and the Landlord is not responsible for loss or damage to anything stored there.

## 16. Noise and quiet enjoyment

Quiet hours are 11 p.m. to 7 a.m. every day. The Tenant and their guests keep noise at a level that does not disturb other residents at any time. The Landlord addresses complaints from other residents about the Tenant in writing, and the Tenant addresses any complaint about other residents to the Landlord in writing.

## 17. Ending the tenancy

Either party may end the tenancy at the end of the term, or at the end of any month once it has become month to month, by giving written notice. The Tenant gives at least 60 days' written notice, and the notice period ends on the last day of a rental month. The Landlord gives notice only for a reason the law permits and with the notice period the law requires for that reason. Notice is given by email to the address each party names in section 21, or by hand. A notice sent by email is received on the day it is sent if sent before 5 p.m. on a business day, and on the next business day otherwise.

## 18. Moving out

At the end of the tenancy the Tenant leaves the premises clean, returns every key and fob, and gives the Landlord a forwarding address. The Landlord and the Tenant inspect the premises together within two days after the Tenant moves out, using the move-in inspection report as the record of the unit's condition. The Landlord returns the pet deposit and any deposit interest owed within fifteen business days after the inspection, with an itemized list of any deductions.

## 19. Abandoned property

Property the Tenant leaves in the premises, the locker, or the parking space more than seventy-two hours after the tenancy ends is abandoned, and the Landlord may dispose of it in accordance with law.

## 20. Rules of the building

The Tenant follows the building rules posted in the lobby, which cover the laundry room schedule, recycling, the bicycle room, and use of the elevator for moving. The Landlord may change the rules with thirty days' written notice when the change is reasonable and applies to every resident.

## 21. Notices

Notices to the Landlord go to notices@orchardlane.invalid or to the property office at 220 Elm Street during business hours. Notices to the Tenant go to jordan.avery@example.invalid or to the premises.

## 22. Entire agreement

This agreement, the building rules, and the move-in inspection report are the entire agreement between the parties. A change to this agreement is valid only in writing signed by both parties. If any part of this agreement is found to be unenforceable, the rest remains in effect.

Signed August 14, 2026.

Orchard Lane Properties Inc., by Priya Raman, Property Manager
Jordan Avery, Tenant
